title: 2026-11-05_Linux.Mirai_Incident_Response_e16
description: Investigate a compromised host infected with the Linux.Mirai trojan, identify its activities, and take appropriate measures to contain and remediate the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has been compromised by the Linux.Mirai trojan. This malware is known to target Linux systems, particularly IoT devices, and is capable of performing DDoS attacks by infecting devices and using them as part of a botnet. Your task is to investigate the compromised host, identify the malware's activities, and take appropriate measures to contain and remediate the threat. Enter the command 'start' to begin the scenario.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity of periodically collecting `/etc/passwd`, home directory listings, and sensitive files, then exfiltrating them to a C2 server. Enter the service name as your answer.
levels.solution:
1. List all services on the system using `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`.
2. Look for unfamiliar service names or misspellings of legitimate services.
3. Check the service descriptions and startup behavior for any unusual activity.
4. Identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
The service name is `dvrHelper.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual descriptions or startup behavior.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The service name is related to network diagnostics.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system for exfiltrating data to a C2 server. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication. Enter the port number as your answer.
levels.solution:
1. Use `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the service configuration.
2. Pay particular attention to the `ExecStart` field, which specifies the path to the script launched by the service.
3. Inspect the script to find the port number used for communication.
The port number is `5556`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the service configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` field in the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is specified in the script launched by the service.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigators suspect that a mechanism keeps the identified service running across reboots and process termination. Determine which system component is responsible for this activity. Enter the timer name as your answer.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers on the system using `systemctl list-timers --all`.
2. Look for timers associated with the identified service.
3. Inspect the timer configuration using `systemctl cat <timer>`.
4. Identify the timer responsible for the recurring execution of the service.
The timer name is `dvrHelper.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers associated with the identified service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The timer name is related to network diagnostics.
